deep_analysis.executive_intro:
This FTSE screen is broadly cautious: 140 holds and 40 avoids outweigh 20 strong buys and 49 buys, so value signals are selective rather than market-wide. Among the five top candidates, three sit in Industrials (FGP.L, MEGP.L, GFTU.L), with Healthcare (HIK.L) and Communication Services (ITV.L) rounding out the list — a tilt toward cyclical and operational businesses rather than financials or tech. All five carry “new” signals (one week at rating) with conviction scores of 39–54%, so quantitative support is fresh and not yet proven over time. Several names were adjusted from strong buy to buy because of FCF or earnings-basis overlays, and multiple tickers show large divergences between filing, screen TTM, and company-adjusted free cash flow — treat headline yields and FCF metrics as provisional until reconciled.

**FGP.L (FirstGroup plc)** — Ten of 22 models passed (composite 91%, sector-relative 86%), spanning cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk families. Key metrics: P/E 9.2, P/B 1.4, yield 3.9%, ROE 16.7%. Passes include Earnings Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Neff PEGY, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, Piotroski F-Score (8/9), Composite Value, and Earnings Quality; failures centre on leverage (D/E 161%), weak liquidity (current ratio 0.73), and FCF Yield (basis mismatch: filing $362.6M vs screen TTM $302.8M vs company-adj £113.5M). Statutory earnings growth is −5.9% while adjusted EPS growth is +16%. Industrials cluster risk applies (one of three industrial names in the top five). **Verdict: watchlist** — attractive headline valuation and cash conversion, but high leverage, liquidity stress, and unresolved FCF definitions argue for filing-level diligence before accumulating.

**MEGP.L (ME Group International plc)** — Fifteen of 22 models passed (composite 84%, sector-relative 89%), the broadest pass rate in the group, with all five factor families clearing. Key metrics: P/E 7.8, P/B 2.2, yield 6.9%, ROE 28.2%, D/E 28%. Passes include Graham Enterprising, FCF Yield, Buffett Quality, Economic Moat, High Dividend Yield, Magic Formula, and Financial Health; failures include Piotroski F-Score (6/9), Earnings Quality (weak free-cash conversion), and Lynch PEG. Interim-quality overlay flagged declining interim EPS and FCF/dividend coverage below 1.0× (gross −0.90×, net 0.84×). Second Industrials name in the top five. **Verdict: watchlist** — deep quantitative support on cheapness and quality, but dividend sustainability and interim deterioration need confirmation before full accumulation.

**HIK.L (Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC)** — Ten of 22 models passed (composite 81%, sector-relative 91%). Key metrics: P/E 12.6, P/B 1.9, yield 3.8%, ROE 15.4%, D/E 77%. Passes include Graham Enterprising, Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, and Financial Health; failures include FCF Yield (3.5% vs 5% threshold), Earnings Yield (7.9% vs 8%), Piotroski F-Score (6/9), and Earnings Quality (weak free-cash conversion). Healthcare price-erosion overlay and FCF basis mismatch (filing $119M vs screen TTM $14.4M) triggered downgrade to buy; statutory earnings growth −4.7%. **Verdict: watchlist** — sector-relative cheapness and quality screens pass, but pricing pressure, weak FCF conversion, and FCF definition divergence warrant caution.

**GFTU.L (Grafton Group plc)** — Twelve of 22 models passed (composite 83%, sector-relative 81%). Key metrics: P/E 12.4, P/B 1.2, yield 3.6%, ROE 8.4%, D/E 38%. Passes include Graham Defensive, Graham Enterprising, Schloss Low P/B, FCF Yield (10.1%), Piotroski F-Score (8/9), Earnings Quality, and Financial Health (CR 2.11, coverage 6.8×); failures include Quality Value and Buffett Quality (ROE 8.4%, thin margins). FCF/dividend coverage is strong (net 2.83×). Timing signal is “wait” with RSI 74 (overbought). Third Industrials name — meaningful sector concentration if building a basket from this screen. **Verdict: accumulate on pullback** — the cleanest balance sheet and Graham-style profile in the group, but wait for better entry given overbought technicals and cyclical building-materials exposure.

**ITV.L (ITV plc)** — Fourteen of 22 models passed (composite 77%, sector-relative 86%). Key metrics: P/E 12.0, P/B 1.6, yield 6.8%, ROE 13.5%, D/E 52%. Passes include Lynch PEG (PEG 0.45, growth 26.7%), High Dividend Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Quality Value, and Financial Health; failures include Piotroski F-Score (3/9), FCF Yield (basis mismatch: filing $148M vs screen TTM $211.9M vs company-adj £325M), and Economic Moat. FCF/dividend coverage is thin (gross 0.36×, net 0.79×); price is below the 200-day MA with RSI 37. **Verdict: watchlist** — compelling income and growth-on-paper metrics, but very weak Piotroski score, uncertain FCF basis, and structural media/advertising cyclicality limit conviction.

- FGP.L: High leverage (D/E 161%) and weak liquidity (current ratio 0.73) are not fully captured by passing value screens; transport/industrial cyclicality and contract-renewal risk are open questions. FCF basis divergence (filing $362.6M vs company-adj £113.5M) may reflect lease, pension, or working-capital adjustments not visible in the screen — pension deficit status is unknown from this data.
- MEGP.L: 6.9% yield with net FCF/dividend coverage 0.84× raises dividend-cut risk; interim EPS decline flagged by overlay. Photo-booth/vending exposure may be economically sensitive — cyclicality not quantified in the screen. Governance and customer-concentration data insufficient.
- HIK.L: Healthcare price-erosion overlay signals generic pricing pressure and margin compression not reflected in headline P/E. FCF fell from $329M to $119M year-on-year; capex at $317M vs OCF $436M suggests heavy reinvestment or capacity build — regulatory and patent-cliff risk for injectables/generics is an open question.
- GFTU.L: Building-materials distributor tied to construction cycles; ROE 8.4% and thin margins (5.4%) suggest limited moat despite Graham passes. RSI 74 and “wait for pullback” timing imply near-term mean-reversion risk. Brexit/regional housing-policy exposure not in screen data.
- ITV.L: Piotroski F-Score 3/9 indicates broad operational deterioration (ROA, leverage, margins, asset turnover all failing). Advertising-revenue cyclicality and streaming-disruption risk are structural, not modelled. High dividend (6.8%) with gross FCF coverage 0.36× is a material sustainability concern; governance and content-investment strategy not assessed.
deep_analysis.red_flags:
NAMES WORTH DEEPER RESEARCH

- FGP.L — Which FCF figure is economically correct (filing $362.6M, screen TTM $302.8M, or company-adj £113.5M), and what drives the gap (leases, pensions, working capital)?
- ITV.L — Is the 6.8% dividend fundable on a normalized FCF basis once content capex and advertising cyclicality are stripped out, and what explains the Piotroski score of 3/9?
- HIK.L — How durable is the generic pricing/margin profile flagged by the healthcare price-erosion overlay, and does the $119M filing FCF reflect a trough or a new run-rate?

documents.name: ME Group International plc
documents.executive_summary: ME Group is a cash-generative operator of ~49,000 self-service vending units (photobooths, laundry, print kiosks) across 16 countries, with a dominant franchise in European photo ID and a fast-growing Wash.ME laundry division. The quantitative screen flags a strong buy on cheapness (P/E ~7.8, yield ~6.9%), quality (ROE ~28%), and balance-sheet strength (net cash, low leverage), but near-term earnings momentum has softened: FY2026 profit before tax guidance was cut to £69–74 million after an April consumer slowdown, and interim free-cash-flow/dividend coverage remains tight. The central debate is whether laundry rollout (ASDA, SNCF/RATP renewals, >1,300 planned installations) and capital returns (8.64p total FY2025 dividend, £18m buyback) outweigh structural photobooth regulatory headwinds (Germany, Japan) and recurring governance/process noise (audit delay, cash-in-transit restatement, terminated strategic review).
documents.investment_thesis:
For a value investor, ME Group offers a rare combination of market leadership, high EBITDA margins (~38% in FY2025), and explicit shareholder returns at a modest earnings multiple. The screen passes 15 of 22 models across five families (cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk), with debt/equity ~28%, current ratio ~1.5×, and filing-aligned FY2025 free cash flow of £25.2 million on operating cash flow of £115.5 million — figures consistent with Yahoo secondary data.

Business quality supports the screen: long-dated site contracts, no customer above 2% of turnover, pricing power in needs-driven categories, and laundry EBITDA margins (~49%) exceeding photobooth (~35%). Wash.ME grew vending revenue 16.3% in H1 FY2026 and now contributes 54% of group EBITDA — a deliberate diversification that improves return on invested capital versus the mature photobooth estate.

The value case is reinforced by capital allocation: FY2025 total dividend rose 9.5% to 8.64p (58% payout), a £18m buyback launched in March 2026 (£4.5m executed by July), and net cash of £26.5m at 31 October 2025 (excluding £13.0m lease liabilities). Management targets acquisitions strictly adjacent to core vending.

However, the screen’s interim-quality overlay (adjusted signal: buy, not strong buy) is warranted: H1 FY2026 diluted EPS fell 3.9% to 6.48p, cash from operations dropped 18.9%, net cash fell to £7.5m, and gross FCF/dividend coverage remains below 1.0×. Piotroski F-Score of 6/9 and failed earnings-quality model flag conversion and balance-sheet trend risks that pure multiple screens underweight.
documents.financial_review:
**FY2025 (31 October 2025)** — primary: `f40be706e75a10ae.txt`, `ir_a006e8bd9b660a9c.txt`, `ir_55af4b8f27e3dd6f.txt`.

Revenue £315.4m (+2.4%); EBITDA £120.4m (+5.4%); PBT £78.2m (+6.5%); PAT £56.6m; diluted EPS 14.91p (+4.5%). Total dividend 8.64p (+9.5%), returning £32.6m; dividends paid £29.8m. Two operating-cash measures coexist: “cash generated from operations” £115.5m (KPI/management metric) vs net cash from operating activities £90.8m (statutory, per Yahoo). Capex £65.6m. Screen/Yahoo FCF £25.2m → net dividend cover **0.84×**; using the filing KPI minus capex (~£49.9m) would imply ~**1.7×** cover — treat headline yield as provisional until reconciled. Net cash £26.5m; borrowings ~£30m; covenants comfortably met (`ir_55af4b8f27e3dd6f.txt`). No customer ≥10% of revenue (`ir_a006e8bd9b660a9c.txt`). Continental Europe 68.3% of revenue (`ir_55af4b8f27e3dd6f.txt`).

**H1 FY2026 (30 April 2026)** — primary: `ac9d0c965a93c3fd.txt`, `ir_3f2f55026f8c6fe6.txt`.

Revenue £154.3m (+0.3%); EBITDA £57.0m (+7.1%); PBT £32.7m (−3.8%); diluted EPS 6.48p (−3.9%). Cash from operations £38.7m (−18.9%); capex £33.9m; implied H1 FCF ~£4.8m before dividends of £14.5m paid plus £2.7m buybacks. Interim dividend cut to 3.60p (−6.5%). Net cash fell to £7.5m. Wash.ME vending +16.3%; Photo.ME −6.2%. FY2026 PBT guidance £69–74m. May vending +11.1% YoY post-April trough.

**Trading update (1 June 2026):** `e5f6ebdd46934d00.txt` — April Photo.ME −17%, laundry +3%; equipment sales −14%.

**Gaps:** FY2026 final dividend undeclared; screen TTM FCF (£15.7m) vs FY2025 (£25.2m) unexplained; OCF definition bridge not extracted from annual-report notes despite `ir_55af4b8f27e3dd6f.txt` being indexed.

documents.risks_and_flags:
**Evidenced (closed or partially closed):**

- **Customer concentration — resolved.** No customer ≥10% revenue; no account >2% turnover (filings above). ASDA partnership (up to 700 machines, `964cf838810978f3.txt`) is largest laundry client but below statutory major-customer threshold.
- **Dividend sustainability — open, partially evidenced.** Management cut H1 interim 6.5%; capital policy permits dividend adjustment (`ir_9ac08315f9388f7e.txt`); FY2025 screen FCF cover 0.84×; competing £18m buyback (`1d660d1c237711ac.txt`) and growth capex absorb cash. Final FY2026 dividend unknown.
- **Cyclicality — open, sensitivity shown.** April 2026 consumer slowdown linked to Middle East conflict (`e5f6ebdd46934d00.txt`, `ir_3f2f55026f8c6fe6.txt`); principal risks acknowledge recession impact on discretionary spending (`f40be706e75a10ae.txt`). No historical recession beta or revenue elasticity quantified; screen cyclical overlay not triggered.
- **Governance — partially open.** Concert Party control complicates buybacks (Rule 9 waiver 83.54%, `40147467451781c7.txt`); audit delay/suspension (`4e623d8eb77b8f49.txt`); two accounting restatements; family executive concentration; auditor reappointment only 83.50% (`e98dc656fdccc24a.txt`). Board independence matrix and related-party detail not in extracted RNS bodies.
- **Financial — evidenced.** Covenants met but include FCF tests (`ir_55af4b8f27e3dd6f.txt`); net cash depleted to £7.5m; Piotroski 6/9 and failed Earnings Quality model (`screening_snapshot.json`).
- **Regulatory — evidenced.** German/Japanese photo-ID rule changes; Photo.ME still ~54% of H1 vending revenue.

documents.name: Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC
documents.executive_summary: Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC is a diversified generic and branded medicines group (Injectables, Hikma Rx, Branded MENA) trading on a modest multiple (screen P/E 12.6, P/B 1.9, yield 3.8%) despite investment-grade balance sheet metrics and a recovering earnings trajectory. FY2025 core operating profit rose 3% to $741m on 6% core revenue growth; H1 2026 accelerated to 9% core profit growth on 4% revenue, with management reiterating full-year core operating profit guidance of $720–770m. The quantitative screen rates the name a strong buy (10/22 models, 81% composite), but overlays already temper this to Buy on healthcare price-erosion, statutory/adjusted EPS divergence, and a material free-cash-flow basis mismatch (filing-aligned FCF $119m vs screen TTM $14m). The central debate is whether Branded momentum and US manufacturing scale can offset Injectables margin compression, elevated capex, and the withdrawal of medium-term guidance following the February 2026 profit reset.
documents.investment_thesis:
For a value investor, Hikma offers a rare combination of cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk-screen passes: P/E below 25, P/B below 3, debt/equity 77%, ROE 15.4%, and five value families cleared (cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk). Business quality is underwritten by segment diversity—Branded is the #1 pharma company by sales in MENA, Injectables is a top-three US generic injectables supplier by volume, and the group carries BBB/stable ratings from S&P and Fitch with net debt/core EBITDA at 1.6x at year-end 2025 (1.9x at H1 2026).

The screen’s strong-buy signal aligns with a business that is growing core earnings, returning capital (84c total dividend in 2025, +5%; $250m buyback launched February 2026), and trading below sector peers on headline multiples. H1 2026 core operating profit of $405m (+9%) and operating cash flow of $214m (+33%) suggest the February guidance cut may have marked a trough rather than structural deterioration. US domestic manufacturing (Ohio, New Jersey) also positions Hikma relatively well versus import-dependent peers if generic drug tariffs materialise—a point echoed in sell-side coverage.

Where the screen is less convincing: FCF Yield, Lynch PEG, Economic Moat, Piotroski F-Score (6/9), and Earnings Quality all fail. Statutory EPS growth is −4.7% while adjusted EPS growth is +1.7%, and FY2025 filing-aligned FCF of $119m covers the dividend only thinly after $317m capex. These are not disqualifiers for a value case, but they explain why deep research should treat the signal as “accumulate on quality at a discount,” not unequivocal strong buy.

documents.name: Grafton Group plc
documents.executive_summary: Grafton Group is a geographically diversified European distributor of construction-related products and DIY retail (Island of Ireland, Great Britain, Northern Europe, Iberia), trading at modest absolute multiples (P/E 12.4, P/B 1.2, yield 3.6%) against a balance sheet that reports £274.0m net cash before lease liabilities and net debt/EBITDA of 0.39× at FY2025. FY2025 revenue rose 10.4% to £2.52bn and adjusted operating profit 7.1% to £190.2m, driven materially by the Salvador Escoda acquisition in Iberia and resilient Irish operations, whilst Great Britain remains cyclically weak into 2026. The quantitative screen flags strong value, quality, dividend, GARP and risk characteristics (Piotroski 8/9, current ratio 2.11), but timing suggests waiting for a pullback (RSI 74). The central debate is whether geographic diversification and disciplined capital return (21.8% share-count reduction since May 2022) offset structurally subdued UK/Northern European construction markets and sub-12% ROE that screens fail on moat/quality models.
documents.investment_thesis:
For a value investor, Grafton offers a rare combination of apparent cheapness, cash conversion and shareholder-friendly capital allocation in a fragmented, consolidation-amenable sector. The screen passes 12 of 22 models across five factor families — Graham Defensive/Enterprising, Schloss Low P/B, Earnings Yield, FCF Yield, Neff PEGY, Dividend Growth, Dreman Contrarian, Piotroski F-Score (8/9), Composite Value, Earnings Quality and Financial Health — with full data quality (20/20 metrics). Cheapness is supported by P/E 12.4 and P/B 1.20; quality by positive and improving cash flows (FY2025 filing-aligned FCF £205.6m per screen; company-reported adjusted FCF £168.3m), FCF dividend coverage of roughly 2.8× net of buybacks, and leverage (D/E 37.6%) well inside management’s investment-grade ceiling of 2.0× net debt/EBITDA.

Business quality complements the screen. Grafton operates ~470 branches under local brands with a federated model, #1 positions in Ireland, and a deliberate pivot toward faster-growing Iberia (Salvador Escoda, Mercaluz). Management has returned £428m via buybacks to FY2025 and guided FY2026 adjusted operating profit of £190–200m despite GB headwinds — implying earnings stability rather than deep cyclical distress. The 2030 Capital Markets Event targets >10% adjusted EPS CAGR and ~13% ROCE, supported by £850m+ cumulative FCF ambition. Failed screen models (Graham Net-Net, Deep Value, Lynch PEG, Buffett/Economic Moat on ROE) correctly flag that this is not a wide-moat compounder at current returns (ROE 8.4%) but rather a cyclically depressed, cash-rich distributor where recovery in GB and Northern Europe could re-rate earnings and ROCE.

rules: Universe: only strong_buy / buy names from the latest screen.
Timing filter: names with timing_signal=wait are excluded from new buys.
Sector cap: at most 1 name(s) per known sector (cap=25%).
Ranking: highest conviction_score first, keep at most 4 names.
Sizing: equal-weight sleeves of current NAV after exits; buys limited by remaining cash.
Costs: 3.0% applied on each buy and sell.
Hold buffer: full exit only after 2 consecutive rebalance(s) outside the target set.
Re-entry cooldown: wait 1 rebalance(s) after a full exit before buying the same name again.
Dust guard: skip trim/top-up adjustments below £10.
